journal_name: IEEE/ACM Transactions on Computational Biology and Bioinformatics

abstracts.abstract: The analysis of biological networks has traditionally relied on static graph representations that fail to capture the dynamic nature of cellular processes. This paper introduces a novel theoretical framework termed Dynamic Hypergraph Analysis for Biological Systems (DHABS), which fundamentally reconceptualizes molecular interaction modeling through time-evolving hypergraphs. Unlike conventional approaches that treat biological networks as simple graphs with pairwise interactions, DHABS represents multi-way molecular associations as hyperedges whose topology changes continuously across experimental conditions or temporal stages. We formalize the mathematical foundations of dynamic hypergraph topology and establish rigorous proofs for key properties including connectivity preservation and temporal stability. The framework enables the derivation of novel centrality measures specifically designed for biological relevance, including pathway influence coefficients and crosstalk intensity metrics. Application to three benchmark datasets encompassing protein-protein interaction networks, gene regulatory circuits, and metabolic pathways demonstrates that DHABS captures emergent properties invisible to traditional analysis methods. Theoretical analysis reveals that the hypergraph representation reduces information loss by approximately 40% compared to graph-based models when modeling complex cellular decisions. This paradigm shift from pairwise to multi-way interaction analysis provides a new mathematical foundation for understanding biological systems where higher-order interactions play critical roles, with implications for drug target identification and disease mechanism elucidation.

Multiple sequence alignment remains a fundamental yet computationally challenging task in computational genomics, where the trade-off between alignment accuracy and algorithmic efficiency continues to drive research innovation. We present a novel progressive alignment algorithm with theoretically guaranteed convergence properties, addressing the longstanding limitation of existing heuristics that lack formal performance bounds. The proposed method, Convergent Progressive Alignment (CPA), employs a sophisticated scoring function integrating substitution matrices, affine gap penalties, and position-specific gap costs derived from amino acid conservation patterns. We establish rigorous theoretical foundations proving that CPA converges to a locally optimal solution with probability approaching one as sequence length increases, providing the first such guarantee for progressive alignment methods. The algorithm introduces an adaptive weighting scheme that dynamically adjusts column weights based on sequence variability, thereby improving sensitivity for conserved functional domains. Complexity analysis demonstrates that CPA achieves O(n²) time complexity compared to O(n³) required by standard progressive methods, while maintaining superior alignment quality on benchmark datasets including BAliBASE and OXBench. Extensive evaluation across 2,400 benchmark alignments shows that CPA improves average accuracy by 8.3% over MUSCLE and 5.7% over MAFFT on distantly related sequences. These results establish CPA as a theoretically principled and practically effective solution for large-scale phylogenetics and functional genomics applications.

The integration of multi-omics data remains a critical challenge in precision medicine, with existing platforms typically treating genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic analyses as separate workflows. This paper introduces MetaOmicsFlow, a comprehensive computational platform that fundamentally reimagines biological data integration through a unified, pipeline-agnostic architecture. The system implements a novel hierarchical data model that maintains semantic relationships across different molecular layers while enabling flexible plugin-based extension for novel omics technologies. MetaOmicsFlow's core innovation lies in its dynamic orchestration engine that automatically optimizes computational resource allocation based on data characteristics and analysis objectives, supporting execution across distributed computing environments including cloud infrastructure and high-performance computing clusters. The platform introduces specialized modules for integrated pathway analysis, cross-platform normalization, and causal inference from heterogeneous biological measurements. We demonstrate the system's capabilities through case studies in cancer biomarker discovery and drug response prediction, where MetaOmicsFlow identified novel multi-omics signatures missed by conventional single-platform analyses. Performance benchmarks indicate that MetaOmicsFlow reduces end-to-end analysis time by 65% compared to existing workflows while improving reproducibility through comprehensive provenance tracking. The platform is designed to serve as infrastructure for both research applications and clinical decision support, addressing the growing need for standardized, scalable multi-omics analysis in biomedical computing.

Drug discovery pipelines increasingly rely on computational screening of vast chemical libraries, yet existing systems struggle with the growing scale of available compounds and the need for rapid virtual screening against multiple protein targets. We present ChemScreen-X, an enhanced virtual screening system that significantly improves throughput and accuracy through innovations in molecular representation, parallel processing, and result integration. The system implements a novel hybrid molecular fingerprint scheme combining structural descriptors with learned embeddings from graph neural networks, enabling more nuanced similarity assessment for diverse chemical scaffolds. ChemScreen-X introduces a hierarchical screening workflow that progressively filters candidate compounds using lightweight computational filters before applying expensive quantum mechanical calculations only to promising candidates. The architecture leverages GPU-accelerated computation and intelligent batching strategies to achieve a 12-fold speedup compared to our previous system while maintaining screening accuracy. We implemented robust consensus scoring that integrates multiple complementary methods including molecular docking, machine learning-based binding affinity prediction, and similarity-based virtual screening. Validation on standard benchmarks including DUD-E demonstrates that ChemScreen-X achieves area under the ROC curve of 0.89 compared to 0.76 for our baseline system. The platform has been deployed for screening over 10 million compounds against several therapeutic targets, identifying 47 novel hit compounds subsequently validated through experimental assays. ChemScreen-X represents a substantial advancement in computational infrastructure for drug discovery and biological data mining.
